paragraphs: In Sunderland the council's fostering service is run by Together for Children, the organisation that has provided the city's children's services since April 2017. You can foster with it or with one of the independent agencies shown above. When Ofsted rated Sunderland's children's services outstanding in 2021, the government said it was the first council to go from failing to the top grade in a single inspection cycle.

The city is also the base for Foster with North East, the recruitment hub that Together for Children leads for twelve North East councils, from Darlington and Hartlepool to Northumberland. Its team works from the Sandhill Centre. Enquire online during opening hours and you should hear back the same day; a fostering social worker answers your early questions, then hands you to your own council for the assessment, ringing at least twice along the way. You can also be paired with an experienced buddy carer.

The hub was set up because the region needs far more carers. It says about 6,000 children are in care across the North East, against roughly 1,500 foster carers. Marking its first year in October 2024, the council said more than 850 people had enquired, that 23.1 per cent of first enquiries had gone on to apply against a national rate of 12 per cent, and that the time from application to approval had fallen to 4.8 months, compared with six months nationally. A government-funded evaluation published in September 2025 found that carers valued the quick replies and the Skills to Foster training.

You must be at least 18, though most services ask for 21. Marriage, sexuality, gender and owning your home do not matter, minor offences need not count against you, and you can work if you can make time for the child, meetings and training. Research the hub publicised found many people wrongly think you need children of your own or a salary of at least £25,000. Each council sets its own pay, and we do not yet have a Sunderland pay page, so ask Together for Children for its current rates.

Fostering for Together for Children means caring for Sunderland's own children; an agency approves and supports you itself and is asked by councils across the region to look after children. Compare the council with two or three of the services above. Nearby, see our pages for South Tyneside, Gateshead, County Durham and Tyne and Wear.
